questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

The diagram shows triangle ABC, not to scale. AB=5 cm, ∠CAB=50° and ∠ACB=112°.
(a) Find BC. [3]
(b) Find the area of triangle ABC. [3]
questions.summary: Use sine rule and triangle area.
questions.solution: By sine rule BC/sin50°=5/sin112°, so BC=4.13 cm. The third angle is B=18°, and AC=5sin18°/sin112°=1.666 cm. Area=(1/2)(5)(1.666)sin50°=3.19 cm².

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 7]

Let f(x)=(6x²−4)/eˣ, for 0≤x≤7.
(a) Find the x-intercept of f. [2]
(b) The graph has a maximum at A. Write down A. [2]
(c) On the grid, sketch f. [3]
questions.summary: Find key features and sketch an exponential-rational function.
questions.solution: Since eˣ>0, 6x²−4=0 gives x=√(2/3)=0.816 on the domain. A calculator maximum gives A=(2.29099,2.78124)≈(2.29,2.78). The sketch starts at (0,−4), crosses at 0.816, reaches A, then decreases toward 0 while remaining positive through x=7.

5. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let f(x)=6−ln(x²+2), for x∈ℝ. The graph passes through (p,4), where p>0.
(a) Find p. [2]
(b) The region enclosed by f, the x-axis and x=−p, x=p is rotated 360° about the x-axis. Find the volume. [3]
questions.summary: Solve a logarithmic equation and calculate a volume numerically.
questions.solution: 4=6−ln(p²+2) gives ln(p²+2)=2, hence p=√(e²−2)=2.32143. The volume is V=π∫_{−p}^{p}[6−ln(x²+2)]²dx=331.989≈332.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

In the expansion of ax³(2+ax)¹¹, the coefficient of the term in x⁵ is 11880. Find a.
questions.summary: Use a binomial coefficient to determine a parameter.
questions.solution: To produce x⁵ after multiplying by ax³, use the x² term of (2+ax)¹¹: C(11,2)2⁹a²x²=28160a²x². Multiplication gives coefficient 28160a³. Thus 28160a³=11880, so a³=27/64 and a=3/4.

8. [Maximum mark: 14]

Data for six hives:
[Table: bees N: 190,220,250,285,305,320; honey P (g): 900,1100,1200,1500,1700,1800.]
Regression model P=aN+b. (a) Find a,b. [3] (b) Estimate P for 270 bees. [2]
A cumulative frequency graph shows monthly production for all 200 hives. [Increasing curve from 600 to 2000 g; it gives 40 hives at 1080 g and 168 hives at 1640 g.]
Types: low P≤1080; regular 1080<P≤k; high P>k.
(c) Write down number low. [1]
128 are regular. (d) Find (i) k; (ii) number high. [5]
(e) Each low hive independently has probability 0.75 of becoming regular. Find P(exactly 30 low hives become regular). [3]
questions.summary: Use regression, cumulative frequency and a binomial model.
questions.solution: Regression gives a=6.96103≈6.96 and b=−454.805≈−455. At N=270, P=1424.67≈1420 g. The graph gives 40 low hives. Regular plus low is 128+40=168; reading the graph gives k=1640 g, leaving 200−168=32 high hives. For X~B(40,0.75), P(X=30)=C(40,30)0.75³⁰0.25¹⁰=0.144.

9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Note: distance is in metres and time in seconds. A particle moves for five seconds with acceleration a=3t²−14t+8, for 0≤t≤5.
(a) Write down t when a=0. [2]
(b) Find all t for which velocity is decreasing. [2]
At t=0 velocity is 3 m s⁻¹. (c) Find velocity v(t). [6]
(d) Find total distance travelled when velocity is increasing. [4]
questions.summary: Integrate acceleration and analyze velocity intervals.
questions.solution: 3t²−14t+8=(3t−2)(t−4), so a=0 at t=2/3 and 4. Velocity decreases where a<0, namely 2/3<t<4. Integrating, v=t³−7t²+8t+C; v(0)=3 gives v=t³−7t²+8t+3. Velocity increases on 0<t<2/3 and 4<t<5. Integrating |v| over these intervals (splitting where needed) gives total distance 14.2191≈14.2 m.

questions.accessible_text:
10. [Maximum mark: 17]

Note: In this question, distance is in millimetres.

Let f(x)=x+a sin(x−π/2)+a, for x≥0.

(a) Show that f(2π)=2π. [3]

The graph of f passes through the origin. Let P_k be any point on the graph of f with x-coordinate 2kπ, where k∈ℕ. A straight line L passes through all the points P_k.

(b) (i) Find the coordinates of P₀ and of P₁.
    (ii) Find the equation of L. [6]

(c) Show that the distance between the x-coordinates of P_k and P_(k+1) is 2π. [2]

Diagram 1 shows a saw. The length of the toothed edge is the distance AB. The toothed edge of the saw can be modelled using the graph of f and the line L, as represented in Diagram 2.

[Diagram 1, not to scale: A saw whose straight toothed edge runs from A to B.]

[Diagram 2, not to scale: Coordinate axes labelled distance (in mm). The line L rises from the origin and the periodic graph of f forms a sequence of arches above L, meeting L at consecutive points P_k and P_(k+1). The shaded region enclosed by f and L between P_k and P_(k+1) is labelled tooth.]

The shaded part on the graph is called a tooth. A tooth is represented by the region enclosed by the graph of f and the line L, between P_k and P_(k+1).

(d) A saw has a toothed edge which is 300 mm long. Find the number of complete teeth on this saw. [6]
questions.summary: Analyze a periodic saw-tooth model and count complete teeth.
questions.solution: f(2π)=2π+a sin(3π/2)+a=2π. At multiples 2kπ, sin(2kπ−π/2)=−1, so P_k=(2kπ,2kπ). Thus P₀=(0,0), P₁=(2π,2π), and L is y=x. Consecutive x-coordinates differ 2(k+1)π−2kπ=2π. Since the 300 mm toothed edge is modelled in the direction of L, its horizontal projection is 300/√2 mm. Dividing this by the horizontal width 2π of one tooth gives 300/(2π√2)=33.7618, so the saw has 33 complete teeth.
